summary:
SPACE TIME CAPSULE – Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational web experience that explores the forgotten equipment and scientific instruments left behind during humanity's exploration of the Moon and Mars.

The project transforms space exploration history into an immersive digital journey, allowing users to discover the stories behind abandoned lunar modules, scientific experiments, Mars rovers, and other exploration technologies.

Through interactive equipment profiles, historical timelines, storytelling experiences, voice narration, and educational quizzes, users can understand why these machines were sent into space, what discoveries they contributed to, and why they were eventually left behind.

Designed primarily for students aged 10–18, the platform makes complex space science accessible, engaging, and enjoyable. By connecting historical NASA missions with interactive storytelling, SPACE TIME CAPSULE encourages curiosity about planetary exploration and highlights the lasting scientific contributions of equipment that continues to shape our understanding of other worlds.
details:
SPACE TIME CAPSULE – Abandoned but Not Forgotten is an interactive educational web application developed to bring attention to the scientific equipment and technologies left behind during human and robotic exploration of the Moon and Mars.

The platform explores nine significant pieces of space exploration history, including the Apollo 11 Lunar Module, Lunar Roving Vehicle, Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP), Lunar Laser Retroreflector, Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity, Mars Sky Crane, and Perseverance Heat Shield.

Each equipment profile provides information about its original purpose, functionality, scientific contributions, mission history, and present status. The platform also introduces an interactive storytelling feature called "A Machine's Last Message", which presents the history of these machines from their own perspective, helping users emotionally connect with the technology that made space exploration possible.

Additional features include historical timelines, interactive quizzes, a searchable equipment explorer, a glossary of space science terminology, saved discoveries, and voice narration.

The website is designed primarily for students aged 10–18, making space science more accessible through interactive learning rather than conventional text-based explanations.

The project was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with browser-based technologies for interactive functionality, animations, and speech narration.

Its creative approach combines space exploration history, digital storytelling, and educational gamification to transform forgotten space equipment into meaningful learning experiences.

The intended impact is to encourage scientific curiosity, improve awareness of NASA's historical missions, and inspire the next generation to explore science, engineering, and space technology.
